body:
Myk settled the design 2026-08-25: an offer token is the pen pattern applied to
federation. This realizes the open halves of T188 (loam_federate_offer) and T196 (where a
runtime-issued federation credential lives) — archive both when this lands, with a note.

THE DESIGN, settled:
- `loam federate offer --container <name> [--label <who-for>]` mints a bearer secret at
  offer.<container>.<label>.token in the HOME (0600, beside the pen seeds — a secret never
  enters the ground) and plants a GRANT delta binding the token's derived identity to a new
  narrow `offer` verb, scoped to that one container.
- The /:mount/federate door accepts the operator token (unchanged) OR a bearer whose derived
  identity holds a surviving `offer` grant covering the requested container. An offer token
  reads ONE container's published deltas and nothing else: no register, no grant-minting, no
  other container, no write.
- Revocation is striking the grant — visible in `loam grant list` (T205's ledger renders it),
  history kept, access dead on the next request.
- `loam_federate_offer` (MCP) mints one behind the existing container-scoped `federate` grant,
  so an agent can offer a channel without ever seeing the operator token. It returns the token
  ONCE; the tool result is the only copy that leaves the home.
- The README's "federating still costs a peer your operator token" wart comes out in the same
  change, replaced by the offer flow, quickstart re-verified on the two-store rig (T210's
  pattern).

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A peer holding only an offer token pulls the offered container's deltas through /federate;
    the same token is refused for any other container, for register, and for every write door
    (two-sided authority). Verify: new test test/federation/offer-token.test.ts over real HTTP.
(b) Striking the offer grant refuses the next pull, names why, and the ledger shows the grant
    struck with its timestamp (the honored-strike reading). Verify: same file + a ledger
    assertion in a new test/cli file (grant-ledger.test.ts is frozen).
(c) The MCP tool mints only behind the federate grant, returns the token once, and the home
    holds it 0600. Verify: new test/server case (federate-mcp.test.ts is not frozen but prefer
    a new file for the seam).
(d) The operator-token path is byte-unchanged for existing callers. Verify: the existing
    federation suites stay green untouched.

Merge tier: MYK'S MERGE — a new credential accepted at a door widens who can read. The PR
states the widening in one line: a named bearer can now read ONE container's offer without
holding the operator token, and nothing else.
title: The offer token — a pen pointed outward (SETTLED DESIGN; final PR is Myk's merge)
